name: World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The fed's own top singles title, already contested by the time this record's held documents begin (an off-panel 27 November 1997 tournament, per the fed's own title history) and still active as the held record ends. Changes hands three times across the read supercards -- Magnus Colby to the Gambler at Spring Slams, the Gambler to EMT at Brawl For It All -- with a fourth change (to the Candyman) attested only by the fed's own later roster note, off-panel.

name: International Championship
epitaph: The fed's own secondary singles title, already active when the held documents begin and still changing hands as they end. Read directly at Spring Slams (Tommy Rifles over James Pillow) and Danger Zone '98 (Drew Mahony retains over Tommy Rifles); several further changes (EMT, Destructo, Johnny Glamour, Drew Mahony, Scottie Extreme) are attested only by the fed's own title-history sheet, off-panel.

name: North Eastern Championship
epitaph: A regional title crowned in the held documents' own first supercard (a tournament final, the Highway Star over Sandy Fields, Spring Slams) and defended twice on-panel (Nevermind over the Candyman at Brawl For It All; the Candyman over Al Robertson at Danger Zone '98, also ending Al Robertson's own Hardcore Championship as a stipulation). Several further changes (to Nevermind, the Candyman, Al Robertson, Magnus Colby) are attested only by the fed's own title-history sheet, off-panel.

name: Can-Am Championship
epitaph: A title built around a standing tournament, crowned for the first time in the held documents (the Trixxster over the Twilight Prince by submission, Danger Zone '98). No further change of hands falls inside the held record.

name: Tag Team Championship
epitaph: The fed's own tag title, already active when the held documents begin. Defended once on-panel (Shwag over With Authority, Spring Slams) before changing hands twice on-panel across the record (the Best of the Best over Team Elite, Brawl For It All; the Goths over the Best of the Best, Danger Zone '98) and once more at the one-year Anniversary Special's own eight-team tournament (Teen Angst over the Goths and the Best of the Best in turn). Two further changes (the Lethal Leaders to Shwag; Shwag's retirement handing the belts to Team Elite) are attested only by the fed's own title-history sheet, off-panel.
